_meta.domain: Include a person only if a historically significant part of that person's contribution is directly to the breeding and improvement of crops or livestock; agricultural genetics as embodied in usable varieties, hybrids, breeds or germplasm systems; soil science, soil classification, fertilisers, plant nutrition or soil-conservation practices; irrigation, drainage, agricultural water management or land reclamation; farm machinery, mechanised cultivation, harvesting or agricultural engineering; practical control of crop pests, weeds, plant diseases or livestock diseases through pesticides, biological control, integrated pest management, vaccination, breeding or other treatments; veterinary medicine applied to livestock production and disease control; food preservation, canning, thermal sterilisation, pasteurisation, refrigeration, freezing or industrial food processing; dairy testing, dairy microbiology, brewing, fermentation and other food-production technologies; nutrition science when it establishes food-composition, dietary, fortification or supply standards; or forestry, silviculture and land-management methods directed toward sustained production. Require the person's contribution to be embodied in a crop variety, hybrid, breed, germplasm system, machine, irrigation system, fertiliser process, pest-control method, veterinary treatment, preservation process, fermentation method, analytical test, food standard, forestry method or comparable agricultural practice rather than in general advocacy or administration. Reject anyone whose principal significance lies in any other field. Reject biologists, geneticists, microbiologists and biochemists whose reputation rests on fundamental discovery without a substantial agricultural, veterinary or food-production application; chemists, chemical engineers and materials scientists whose work has no central agricultural or food purpose; physicians and nutritionists whose significance is principally clinical rather than in food production, preservation, composition or supply; ecologists, conservationists and environmental campaigners whose contribution is primarily ecological theory, protection, advocacy or policy rather than agricultural, forestry or land-management technique; economists, agricultural policymakers, extension administrators and ministers whose importance is institutional, economic or political; landowners, estate improvers and gentleman farmers whose significance is proprietorial rather than technical; botanists and taxonomists whose work is descriptive rather than directed toward crop improvement or production; zoologists whose work lacks a livestock, veterinary or pest-management application; civil and mechanical engineers whose principal achievements are unrelated to agricultural production, irrigation or land reclamation; chefs, food writers and culinary figures; and industrialists, food-company founders, merchants and executives whose importance is commercial or organisational rather than technological.
_meta.name: agriculture and food technology
